Follow these steps to enable Soft Braille Keyboard, make it the default keyboard and choose a braille table. Braille display screen output is optional and only needed if you use a braille display.
First enable the keyboard in Android, make it the default input method and choose the braille translation tables and keyboard layout you want to start with.

Now calibrate and test the on-screen braille keyboard directly in the practice field below. You can calibrate with all six fingers at once or by holding the first three fingers and then the other three after the prompt.
Choose the speech engine, voice and speaking parameters here so the keyboard is immediately usable after the wizard.
Finish the typing preferences, automatic update checks, crash prompts and optional braille display settings for this user profile.

Calibration: open Soft Braille Keyboard in the field below, then either hold all six fingers at once or hold your first three fingers until you hear the prompt and then hold the other three fingers. After that, type a few characters in the practice field.

Use this form to send a crash or hardware report. The app sends it to the report server first and falls back to a prefilled GitHub issue only when the server upload fails.
